additional_concerns: Candidates node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e, node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f, node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5 and node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 place offering or promotional-link conditions in scope. Their runtime therefore returns OUT_OF_SCOPE rather than FALSE when those conditions fail, although the typed prohibition questions define FALSE as not caught. This scope convention needs reconciliation; it is separate from the paragraph 2.3 claim.

The offer-level candidates combine an offer-level promotional link with an existential non-discount gift classification. Establish that the identified gift component shares the relevant promotional link; otherwise an unrelated component could be caught solely because another part of the offer promotes a product.

The supplied circular supports the gift rule's stated exception, but does not establish general permission or overall compliance for discounted or non-gift benefits. The compliance candidate must remain confined to the selected gift control.

Paragraph 3.11 of the Code of Conduct and the answer to question 1 of the SFC's 30 September 2010 frequently asked questions, identified in footnote 3, are not supplied as external dependencies. Their absence limits independent verification of gift classifications and product-type interpretation; no dependency IDs can be assigned.
No concrete effective interval is supplied in the source text. The candidates' temporal-basis declaration does not independently establish applicability at a particular assessment date.
